title: Early-token prefetch & KV-cache scheduling — integration notes
content:
Purpose:
This note captures design ideas, heuristics, and rollout steps for an "early-token prefetch" optimization that proactively warms the KV cache and opportunistically schedules kernels ahead of time for likely next-token branches. The goal is to reduce tail token latency for chat-style workloads without materially increasing cost or harming output fidelity.

Context and motivation:
- Observed long-tail latency stems from cache misses and on-the-fly kernel selection when sequence contexts hit previously unseen token prefix shapes (lengths, attention patterns).
- For many chat workloads, the next token distribution has a small effective support in the short term (repetitive assistant prompts, constrained system tokens). We can speculatively fetch KV entries and pre-select lightweight kernels to shave tens of milliseconds at the tail.
- Tradeoffs: additional GPU memory pressure, transient extra kernel load, possibility of wasted work and slight throughput drop if mis-speculated.

Key ideas (high level):
1) Predictive KV prefetch: for a request, evaluate a compact heuristic (n-gram, cache-hit history, last-token entropy) to decide whether to prefetch KV rows for the top-K next-token candidates. Store prefetch priority metadata with request context.
2) Kernel priming: simultaneously compile/prepare the small set of kernels that are most likely needed next (e.g., attention path for short vs long sequence; fused attention vs fallback). Keep primed kernels in a hot set per-GPU.
3) Opportunistic batching window: allow a tiny, configurable micro-window (0-8ms) to coalesce adjacent speculative prefetches to avoid duplicated transfers.
4) Backpressure & fast cancel: if later model decisions diverge, prefetch and kernel priming can be aborted or deprioritized immediately to free memory.

Detailed heuristics for prefetch decision (initial WIP):
- Score_S = alpha * recent_kv_hit_rate(context_prefix) + beta * (1 - predicted_next_entropy) + gamma * model_size_penalty + delta * user_tier_boost
- Use thresholds: if Score_S > T_prefetch then prefetch top-N candidate kv rows (N=3 default), else skip.
- Coefficients (alpha/beta/gamma/delta) are tunable via experiment flags; default alpha=0.6, beta=0.3, gamma=-0.1, delta=0.2 for premium customers.
- Predicted_next_entropy computed by a lightweight cached n-gram LM or a tiny on-device classifier trained on request traces (privacy filtered).

KV caching specifics:
- Prefetch granularity: prefetch per-layer KV blocks (not individual token embeddings) to align with our runtime memory pages.
- TTL semantics: speculative entries get shorter TTL (e.g., 5s) and lower priority for eviction.
- Accounting: attribute the memory transient cost to the originating request for billing/experiment metrics, but exclude from normal usage-based billing until confirmation of hit.

Kernel selection and priming:
- Maintain a small LRU of compiled kernels (hot-set) per GPU node. Mark primed kernels with a "soft lock" that prevents eviction for a configurable time window (default 20ms).
- Kernel priming only for lightweight variants: fused attention, optimized matmul for common shape, etc. Do not prime heavyweight compilation tasks (PTX->SASS) speculatively.
- Eviction policy: if memory pressure exceeds X% (configurable, default 78%), cancel pending priming and evict low-priority speculative kernels first.

Scheduling integration (runtime changes):
- Extend request descriptor with speculative_metadata: {prefetch_candidates, prefetch_priority, primed_kernels} (implementation note: store as flattened tags in the descriptor header).
- Scheduler must be able to schedule speculative prefetch tasks on separate lanes that have lower QoS than confirmed token work. These lanes may be throttled under load.
- Provide a fast-cancel API so that downstream token generation can cancel outstanding speculative tasks on divergence.

Acceptance criteria (for rollout to canary/Dedicated):
- Latency: 99th percentile per-token generation latency reduced by >=10% for targeted chat workloads on canary fleet. Measure both host-side and GPU-side token latency.
- Cost: incremental GPU memory usage increase <= 5% on average across canary nodes. If average goes above 7%, fail gating.
- Correctness: output token distributions must not regress materially. Use a prompt-set of 2k deterministic evals and measure top-1 token agreement with baseline; target agreement >= 99.5%.
- Stability: no increase in GPU OOM, no increase in fatal serving exceptions.
- Hit efficiency: ratio of speculative-prefetch hits to prefetch attempts >= 0.35 in first canary window.

Rollback triggers (automated):
- If any of the following hold for 10-minute sliding window, initiate automatic rollback off the canary fleet and revert traffic:
  - 99p token latency increases vs baseline by >5% (unexpected regression).
  - OOM or kernel compile failures > 0.05% of requests.
  - Speculative prefetch cost > threshold and hit efficiency < 0.05.
  - Output fidelity regression (measured by top-1 agreement) falls below 98.5%.

Measurement plan and dashboards:
- New metrics to emit per-request: speculative_attempted (bool), speculative_hits (int), speculative_bytes_fetched (int), speculative_kernels_primed (int), speculative_cancelled (bool), speculative_latency_ms (ms).
- Aggregates: speculative_hit_rate, avg_speculative_bytes_per_attempt, spec_mem_pct_of_node, speculative_cpu_ms, speculative_gpu_ms, kernel_priming_fail_rate.
- Dashboards: per-fleet and per-model breakdown; compare canary vs baseline fleet side-by-side.

Experimentation strategy (staged rollout):
1) Local dev builds: unit tests for cancel path, fake KV pages, simulate eviction.
2) Internal dogfood: 0.5% internal traffic, short TTL, metrics only. Observe hit-rate and memory.
3) Canary: 2 dedicated nodes serving small percentage of external traffic with full metrics, acceptance gating enabled.
4) Graded ramp: 2 -> 10 -> 50% of dedicated pool, reevaluate at each stage.

Operational playbook (oncall steps):
- If spec_mem_pct_of_node spikes: reduce speculative TTL to 1s and throttle prefetches by 50% via runtime flag.
- If kernel_priming_fail_rate rises: disable priming, keep prefetching only.
- If fidelity regression detected: switch to oblivious mode (no speculative prefetch) for affected models and collect traces for offline analysis.

Open questions / unknowns (to investigate):
- How well will prefetching generalize to open-ended generation tasks (long creative outputs)? Might be mostly beneficial for bounded token tasks like chat/assistants.
- Cost accounting: how do we fairly charge for wasted speculative work on shared Dedicated nodes? Need finance/product input.
- Privacy: confirm prefetch classifier training pipeline doesn't expose PII; need legal sign-off.
- Multi-tenant memory isolation: ensure speculative TTL/priority can't be exploited to starve other tenants.

Implementation checklist (MVP scope):
- [ ] Descriptor metadata extension + serialization format.
- [ ] Lightweight prefetch decision module (pluggable policy).
- [ ] KV prefetch API and short TTL semantics.
- [ ] Kernel priming lightweight path + soft lock.
- [ ] Throttled speculative lanes in scheduler + cancel API.
- [ ] Metrics emission and dashboard templates.
- [ ] Canary rollout automation and rollback hooks.
- [ ] Unit and load tests simulating mis-speculation flood.

Example sequence (illustrative):
1) Request arrives with context C (user+system+history).
2) Prefetch policy scores C -> decides top-3 token candidates t1,t2,t3.
3) Prefetch fetches KV blocks for tokens (speculative_tiers), priming the common fused-attention kernel for shapes matching len(C)+1.
4) Model generates token t1; if t1 in prefetched top-3, immediate KV hit -> sub-ms improvement on token step; else cancel remaining speculative tasks.

Notes to reviewers (quick asks):
- Please sanity-check the acceptance thresholds and the 35% target hit-rate. If you have better baseline numbers from production traces, paste them into the JIRA linked above.
- Suggest concrete values for TTL and memory thresholds from SRE perspective.
- Thoughts on whether we should bill speculative bytes as "ephemeral" or attribute to the customer for visibility.

This document is intentionally light on final numbers — needs trace-driven tuning. The implementation should be feature-flagged and observability-first so we can experiment rapidly and safely.

-- Priya
(last updated 2025-11-02)
